heard: In March 1888, mild spring weather instantly became a blinding whiteout. At midnight, a brutal nor'easter struck New York City. Temperatures plunged rapidly as rain turned to snow. Winds whipped towering snowdrifts up to 50 feet high. Thousands of passengers remained trapped on frozen elevated trains. Over 200 people froze to death before normal life resumed. In March 1888, mild spring weather instantly became a blinding whiteout.
